To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
A splice-junction mutation that removes exon 65 sequences results in reduced type V collagen production and is associated with the severe form of EDS type I.
a splice-junction mutation of COL5A2 results in the gravior form of EDS type I.

we have identified the first COL5A1 gene mutation in a patient with EDS I, that the COL5A1 mutation results in the removal of 78 amino acids from the pro alpha 5(V) chain carboxyl pro-peptide, and that the COL5 A1 mutation results in reduced type V collagen expression in cultured fibroblasts.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how the mutations we have described in COL5A2 and COL5A1 result in the clinical manifestations of EDS type II and EDS type I, respectively.
the molecular genetics of the Ehlers Danlos syndrome (ED).
understanding the molecular basis of EDS and the role of collagen V in normal and abnormal connective tissue development and maintenance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the COL5A1 locus is a candidate gene for EDS I but not the only one.
the EDS I phenotype is not caused by a single gene defect.
EDS I is genetically heterogeneous with mutations in both COL5A2 and COL5A1 being responsible for the disorder.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
mutations in COL5 genes are a cause for EDS I in a significant number of cases.
COL5A1 is the major locus for EDS I but that other loci are also involved in some cases.
COL5A1 mutations are responsible for some cases of EDS I, but other genes are also responsible for the disorder.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Ehlers Danlos Syndrome is a heterogeneous disorder with multiple causative mutations in the genes that encode the collagen proteins.
mutations in the genes encoding type V collagen are associated with a subset of patients with EDS type I.
the COL5A1 locus is linked to the gravis form (type I) of Ehlers-Denlos syndrome in some families, but that this is not the only locus that is linked to this form.
